title: Bacterial Depletion Protocol for Aiptasia Anemones to Generate Gnotobiotic Hosts
author: Ruben M Costa
license_note: Confirmed via CrossRef DOI metadata: dx.doi.org/10.17504/protocols.io.7mrhk56
materials: Prepare Artificial seawater (ASW) by mixing reagents in MilliQ water and adjusting the pH of the final volume to 8.0-8.2. Filter through 0.22 µm pore size filter.
To prepare the decapsulated Artemia cysts:

steps.title: Prepare Antibiotic Solution (ABS)
steps.instruction: Prepare the antibiotic solution (ABS) by mixing antibiotics with ASW.

substeps.instruction: Sterile filter the final solution through 0.22 µm pore size filters.
Cover the bottle with aluminum foil to protect from light.

steps.title: Prepare Saturated Brine Solution
steps.instruction: Prepare a saturated brine solution by mixing at least 35% w/v (preferably >40%) of NaCl in MilliQ water.

substeps.instruction: Autoclave 80 ml of the solution.
Ensure the solution has a substantial amount of precipitated salts to account for water released from hydrated cysts.

steps.title: Decapsulate Artemia Cysts
steps.instruction: Process Artemia cysts to remove the outer shell and deplete bacteria.

substeps.instruction: Weight 2g of cysts and mix with 150 ml of tap water; hydrate with aeration for 1h.
Add 150 ml of bleach to the cysts and mix with aeration for 4-6 minutes (do not aerate vigorously).
Monitor color change from brown to white, then orange; do not exceed 5-6 minutes to ensure viability.
Strain orange cysts in a 63 µm strainer and rinse extensively under tap water for at least 1 min (or until bleach smell is gone).
Rinse cysts for an additional 30 sec in MilliQ water.

steps.title: Sterilize and Store Cysts
steps.instruction: Treat cysts with ABS and store in brine to prevent hatching.

substeps.instruction: Pour cysts into a 50 ml polypropylene tube in a biosafety cabinet and add ABS until covered.
Incubate in a tilting lab mixer (or belly dancer) for 30 min.
In a biosafety cabinet, strain the cysts and scoop them into the cool autoclaved saturated brine solution.
Store cysts in the fridge at 4°C (stable for up to 4 months). Ensure salt remains precipitated to keep cysts dehydrated.

steps.title: Hatch Cysts and Verify Sterility
steps.instruction: Hatch the sterilized cysts and confirm the absence of bacteria.

substeps.instruction: In a biosafety cabinet, shake the brine to suspend cysts, let salts settle for a few seconds, and take 1 ml of suspension.
Mix the 1 ml suspension with 35 ml of ASW in a 50 ml falcon tube (or scale up using a sterile hatching system) and incubate at RT with agitation.
Allow cysts to hatch for 24-48h.
After 48h, plate 200 µl of hatching water in Marine Agar or rich marine media and incubate for 5 days at 25°C.
If colonies appear, repeat hatching using ABS instead of ASW.

steps.title: Prepare Aiptasia for Depletion
steps.instruction: Rear Aiptasia polyps on a sterile diet before starting the depletion process.

substeps.instruction: Transfer polyps to a clean container in a 12h light:12h dark incubator (20–40 µmol photons m−2 s−1 PAR) at 25ºC using only ASW.
Feed twice a week with decapsulated Artemia nauplii for at least one month, changing water the day after each feeding.
Always open decapsulated cyst stocks under sterile conditions.

steps.title: Initial Surface Decontamination
steps.instruction: Remove surface bacteria and parasitic eukaryotes from Aiptasia polyps (approx. 5mm oral disk).

substeps.instruction: Wash polyps individually and sequentially in two petri dishes with ASW by pipetting up and down with a plastic Pasteur pipette until mucus is released.

steps.title: Antibiotic Treatment of Polyps
steps.instruction: Perform a 7-day antibiotic treatment in a sterile environment (biosafety cabinet).

substeps.instruction: Transfer polyps from ASW to a petri dish containing ABS.
Wash animals once more in ABS and leave in the plate for ~15 min.
Transfer each polyp to a 24-well plate (1 polyp per well) and fill with 1 ml of ABS.
Allow polyps to adhere for a few hours; check for parasites via inverted microscope and wash again with ABS if necessary.
Treat for 7 days at 25°C under normal light cycle with daily media exchange.
During exchanges, clean the bottom of wells with sterile cotton tip swabs wet with 70% Ethanol in MilliQ water, then rinse once with ASW.
Initiate treatment and ASW exchange at the start of the dark cycle to prevent photodegradation of antibiotics (e.g., Rifampicin).
If using high-ventilation incubators, place plates in a zip lock bag with a wet piece of paper to prevent evaporation.

steps.title: Recovery and Final Wash
steps.instruction: Recover treated animals in sterile ASW.

substeps.instruction: Recover animals in ASW for 1 day, washing and exchanging the ASW twice.

steps.title: Verify Bacterial Depletion
steps.instruction: Confirm the success of the treatment using culture and molecular methods.

substeps.instruction: Rinse and lysate individual polyps using a pestle after recovery in ASW.
Plate 50-100 µl of lysates and a drop of water from each well on Marine Agar or rich marine medium; incubate for 5 days at 25°C. Absence of growth indicates success.
Perform DNA extraction on remaining lysate and run a 16S rRNA gene PCR (30 cycles) using 10 ng of DNA template.
Use the following PCR profile: 95°C for 15 min; 30 cycles of (30s at 95°C, 90s at 55°C, 90s at 72°C); final extension at 72°C for 10 min.
Verify success via gel electrophoresis (absence of amplification or levels comparable to negative control).
